Density contours as GateLab draws them

Source: R/strategy_contour.R
gatelabContour.Rd

Computes the contour lines and the outlier points of a biaxial plot by the recipe GateLab's contour mode uses, so a figure made in R matches the app's Gating, Strategy and Illustration plots. The events are placed in a square pixel space (ref_size, the app's Gating plot), binned and smoothed as d3.contourDensity() does (linear binning on a 4-pixel grid, three box blurs each way), and contoured at log-spaced levels from threshold percent of the peak density up to the peak. Points outside the lowest contour are returned as outliers.

Usage

gatelabContour(
  x,
  y,
  xlim,
  ylim,
  levels = 10,
  threshold = 5,
  bandwidth = NULL,
  ref_size = 560
)

Arguments

x, y

Numeric vectors of the events to draw, in display units (for mass cytometry, the arcsinh-transformed values). Give the events the app would draw, for example from gatelabDisplayEvents.

xlim, ylim

The axis ranges of the plot, each c(low, high). The density is estimated in the plot's pixels, so the ranges change the contours.

levels

Number of contour levels, 2 to 30 (the app's "Contour levels").

threshold

Lowest level as a percentage of the peak density (the app's "Contour threshold").

bandwidth

Kernel bandwidth in reference pixels. NULL takes the app's rule, max(2, min(10, round(1200 / sqrt(n)))) for n events on the plot.

ref_size

Side of the square pixel space the density is estimated in.

Value

A list: paths, a data frame of contour lines (x, y, group, level) in data units; outliers, a data frame (x, y) of the events outside the lowest contour; levels, the density levels; bandwidth; and n, the events on the plot.

Details

Ported from d3-contour 4 (density.js) and d3-array 3 (blur.js) as shipped in d3 7.9.0, and from GateLab's _drawContour. Two differences remain: d3 accumulates in single precision, and the app finds outliers on a 256-pixel raster of the lowest contour where this function tests each point against the contour itself.

See also

gatelabPanelGrob, which draws them.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- c(rnorm(2000, 1), rnorm(2000, 4))
y <- c(rnorm(2000, 4), rnorm(2000, 1))
contours <- gatelabContour(x, y, xlim = c(-1, 7), ylim = c(-1, 7))
length(unique(contours$paths$level))
#> [1] 10
nrow(contours$outliers)
#> [1] 62
